name: Queenstown
description: Queenstown on Lake Wakatipu, the adventure capital of the south: the Skyline Gondola up Bob's Peak, the old steamer Earnslaw at its wharf, and the Remarkables across the water.

imagery.attribution: LINZ Queenstown 0.1m Urban Aerial Photos (2026), Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand (CC BY 4.0)

terrain.attribution: LINZ Otago - Queenstown LiDAR 1m DEM (2021), Toitū Te Whenua LINZ, Landpro and Queenstown-Lakes District Council (CC BY 4.0)

datum_note: Lake Wakatipu's level when the LiDAR was flown on 12 March 2021: the median DEM height (NZVD2016) of the ground along the survey's water edge, 309.2 m. The lake's normal operating range is about a metre either side; the scene's 0 m is this level.

water.note: Lake Wakatipu, with Queenstown Bay and Frankton Arm mapped as bays inside it. The lake is 309 m above the sea, so the scene's 0 m is its surface (datum_offset_m); past the frame the lake carries on as open water to the horizon, and the far land rises out of it.

waves.note: A light south-westerly down the lake's reach from Cecil Peak to the town, chosen values, not a measurement. The lake is mostly glassy at dawn and ruffled by afternoon.

water.colour_note: Lake Wakatipu is glacial and very clear (Secchi depths of 10 m and more): a saturated blue in the open lake and turquoise over the shallows off the beaches and the Gardens. Matched to photographs from Bob's Peak and the Fernhill side of the bay, which the owner set as the reference, and to the 2026 LINZ aerial photo.

seawall.note: Queenstown's lake front: grey schist rubble walls and concrete along Marine Parade and the wharves; the lake rises and falls by about a metre with the seasons, not with a tide.

tussock.note: Tussock (trees.json tussock, #286): in the Skyline deck's planted bed, and on the open hills above the town where no canopy stands, off the roads and their houses; denser round the Skyline site, where the game starts.

trees.note: Species are not mapped; the mix is a guess at Queenstown's planting: Douglas fir and other conifers on Bob's Peak and in the Gardens (drawn as the shared pine and sugi), oaks, sycamores, poplars and willows (drawn as the elm and maple) on the streets and the lake front, and a few eucalypts. The woods on Ben Lomond's lower slopes are wilding conifers.

night.note: Queenstown's streets read warm amber in long exposures from Bob's Peak (the reference photograph); the lamps' colours are chosen to match it.

sources.landmarks: TSS Earnslaw, Skyline Gondola, Eichardt's and St Peter's: published dimensions and photographs

relief.name: LINZ New Zealand Contour-Interpolated 8m DEM (CC BY 4.0), read at 32 m

far.note: The Remarkables, Cecil and Walter Peaks and Ben Lomond are the town's backdrop, so the land past the frame is finer here than the default (70 m cells to 36 km, a 640-line grid) and its relief is LINZ's bare-earth national DEM rather than the global surface model. The air over the lake is very clear, so the haze's distances are stretched (clarity 2.2), a chosen value matched to photographs from Bob's Peak.

game.title: Queenstown on Foot
game.blurb: Walk Queenstown's lakefront under the real sun. Sail on the steamer Earnslaw, ride the Skyline Gondola up Bob's Peak, and watch the Remarkables turn pink at dusk.
game.ferry_note: The Earnslaw sails from Steamer Wharf, where she really berths, to the Walter Peak wharf in Beach Bay, 12.5 km across Lake Wakatipu past the map's edge, at her service speed of 13 knots: about half an hour, where the real cruise takes 45 minutes. F skips ahead; at a landing you can skip the wait.

ferry_style.note: The TSS Earnslaw: a snow-white hull and a bright red funnel since her 1984 refit (Wikipedia; RealNZ). 51.2 m by 7.3 m.

cars.note: Queenstown's taxis are mostly white or black cars with a roof sign; the town's buses are white with blue (approximate).

gondola.name: Skyline Gondola
gondola.note: Ten seats, 438 m up to Bob's Peak.
gondola.source: Doppelmayr D-Line detachable gondola opened 29 June 2023: 35 ten-seat Omega V cabins, up to 5 m/s, 760 m inclined, 438 m rise (Doppelmayr release, June 2023; lift-world.info). The cabins: light silver-grey Omega V shells with dark glazing bands (a 2023 photograph of the terminals, Thermosash), their roofs white in LINZ's 2026 aerial photographs.

npcs.name: Aroha
idle: The lake rises and falls a few centimetres every half hour or so. Our tīpuna said it was a giant breathing under the water.
Tāhuna means the shallow bay. That's it below you, between the town and the Gardens.

npcs.name: Callum
idle: She burns about a tonne and a half of coal there and back. You can walk through the engine room and watch the stokers.
Lady of the Lake, they call her. Launched at Kingston in 1912, and still steaming.
Walter Peak's a high-country station. The Colonel's Homestead is up from the wharf, in gardens they've been planting since the 1870s.

npcs.name: Mei
idle: Ten seats a cabin, and the doors close on their own. Mind your feet at the top.
The cabins come round every few seconds, all day and into the evening.

npcs.name: Hemi
idle: The Remarkables run north and south, so they catch the last of the sun from the west. Wait for it.
Ben Lomond's behind us, the big one. You can walk up from here, but take a jacket.

npcs.name: Sophie
idle: On a clear day you can see Walter Peak and Cecil Peak from right over the bay. The lake does the rest.
Down the lake past the peninsula and back: ten minutes and the best view in Otago.

npcs.name: Ana
idle: We come up for the light. Watch the Remarkables go pink when the sun's behind Walter Peak.
My nana worked the gondola in the seventies. Four-seater cabins then, painted orange.

npcs.name: Tom
idle: Lamb from Central Otago and a pinot from Gibbston. Can't go wrong.
The deck's new this year. You can see right down the luge track.

npcs.name: Priya
idle: First time in Queenstown. The lake's bluer than the photos.
We're doing the Earnslaw tomorrow, out to Walter Peak.

npcs.name: Rawiri
idle: Kia ora! The buffet's open till nine. The mussels are from the Marlborough Sounds.
Best table's the corner by the glass. You get the Remarkables and the town both.

npcs.name: Margaret
idle: The stone came off the lake shore in 1932. My grandfather carted some of it.
The east window's the Call of St Peter. It's for the parish's men lost in the war.

npcs.name: Reverend David
idle: Welcome. The church is open every day. The first St Peter's here was timber, in 1863.
The roof's rimu and the font's older than the building. Have a look round.

npcs.name: Lucy
idle: This is one of the oldest houses in Queenstown, 1864. The schist chimney's original.
The flood in 1999 came right up to the verandah. The lake's only across the road.

lines.title: Report back
lines.on_open: The lake, the hill and the air. Go back to Aroha by the glass lift, on the luge track under the deck.

quests.title: Welcome to Tāhuna
talk: Kia ora, welcome to Queenstown! I'm Aroha. This is the view everyone comes for: the town, the bay, the Gardens, and the Remarkables across the lake. It's {season}, and it looks good {now}.

Three ways to know it, any order. The hill: Hemi, along the hillside, knows when the light is best. The lake: Callum, at Steamer Wharf, can get you on the Earnslaw. The air: Sophie keeps a helicopter on the flat above the luge.
The gondola takes you down to Brecon Street. WASD to walk, E to talk, T to switch walks. Which first?

choices.text: The hill: Hemi, along the hillside
The lake: Callum, at Steamer Wharf
The air: Sophie, above the luge

quests.title: Lady of the Lake
talk: Morning! That's her alongside: the Earnslaw, built in Dunedin, carried in pieces by rail to Kingston and launched there in 1912.
Fifty-one metres, twin screws, two triple-expansion engines and the coal to feed them. Thirteen knots, flat out.
She's off to Walter Peak, across the lake under Cecil Peak. Walk round the promenade deck on the way and look back at the town.

steps.text: Sail on the Earnslaw from Steamer Wharf to Walter Peak
Walk up to the Colonel's Homestead

quests.title: The lakefront
talk: Good trip? Now the town from the shore. Walk along Marine Parade past Eichardt's, the old hotel on the corner. It began as William Rees's woolshed.
Keep going round the beach to Williams Cottage, from the 1860s and hardly changed, then out along the Gardens to the point.

steps.text: Walk past Eichardt's on Marine Parade
Walk out to the point of the Queenstown Gardens

quests.title: The Remarkables at dusk
talk: Kia ora. Look across the lake: that's the Remarkables, and Cecil and Walter Peaks down to the right.
Sun goes down at {sunset} today. Stay up here till then and watch the range turn pink. The town's lights come on under you.
Then take the gondola down. Mei at the bottom station will tell you about the ride.

steps.text: Watch the sun go down from Bob's Peak
Ride the gondola down to Brecon Street
Find Mei at the bottom station

quests.title: Up Bob's Peak
talk: Good ride? It drops {landmark:skyline_gondola.rise_m} m between here and the top station, one of the steepest lifts of its kind anywhere.
Go back up whenever you like; the cabins come round every few seconds. Aroha's at the top.

steps.text: Ride the gondola back up to Bob's Peak

quests.title: Over the bay
talk: Hi! She's ready on the pad. Take her down over the town, round the Gardens and out over the bay.
The town's small from up there and the mountains aren't. Bring her down on the Recreation Ground by the lake.

steps.text: Fly over the bay and land back on the Recreation Ground

quests.title: Tāhuna
talk: The lake, the hill and the air. You've done in a day what most visitors take a week over.
The town's yours: change the time, take the steamer again, or go back up the hill for the stars. Winter nights here are very clear.

game.start_note: On the Skyline deck on Bob's Peak, along the restaurant's south-east face, where Queenstown's best-known photograph is taken: the town, Queenstown Bay, the Gardens peninsula, the Kelvin Peninsula and the Remarkables over the lake. The glass lift at the deck's south-west end goes down to the luge track, where Aroha waits.

look.note: Matched to the owner's reference photographs from Bob's Peak: a saturated blue hour with the town's warm lights, and a clear, vivid day.

game.drive_note: Skyline Road, the service road up Bob's Peak, is mapped as a track, and so is the unnamed track that carries it down to Lomond Crescent in Fernhill. The game drives both (drive_named, drive_tracks), so a taxi can come to the top.

outposts.name: Walter Peak
outposts.note: The Earnslaw's far wharf in Beach Bay, in front of the Colonel's Homestead, 13 km across Lake Wakatipu: past the frame, so it is a tile of its own (pipeline/outposts.py).

tour.title: Queenstown from Bob's Peak
tour.text: Kāi Tahu called this shallow bay Tāhuna. Gold brought the town in 1862; now it's bungy, jet boats and ski fields. Across the lake the Remarkables catch the last light of the day.

tour.title: The bay from the Fernhill side
tour.text: Queenstown Bay, the Gardens peninsula and Frankton Arm, with the Remarkables beyond. Watch for the Earnslaw's black smoke as she leaves Steamer Wharf.

tour.title: The Skyline Gondola
tour.text: Up the face of Bob's Peak to the lookout, where the luge tracks wind down the hill and the whole lake lies below. Ride up for sunset and stay for dinner.

tour.title: Steamer Wharf
tour.text: The TSS Earnslaw has sailed from here since 1912, a coal-fired twin-screw steamer still stoked by hand. Take her across to Walter Peak for a high-country farm visit and a sing-along at the piano.

tour.title: The lakefront in winter
tour.text: Marine Parade, the town's lakeside lawn. Even at noon in midwinter only {sun:Marine Parade Reserve|6-21|12:00}% of it is in the sun under the hill, so grab a hot chocolate and walk.
